articles.title: The Blood of Dawnwalker Modders Aren’t Missing the Point – They Just Love the Game
articles.summary: Modders are extending The Blood of Dawnwalker's 30-day time limit to allow more time to complete every questline. But while this goes against the developer's vision, it shouldn't be seen as vandalism.
body: This is an IGN opinion piece from Mat Jones, who thinks everyone’s made too big a deal out of experience-altering mods, and wouldn’t replay a video game ever, even if he were forced to do so by vampires holding his family hostage.

I’ve spent the weeks since The Blood of Dawnwalker’s release nodding at headlines about how the time-pressured quest to rescue lead character Coen’s family – which is on a controversial 30-day timer – is the heart of the design, and that anyone looking to extend that clock with a mod wouldn’t be having the intended experience.

But, after reading that the developers themselves aren’t so bothered about the timer that they’d definitely want to add it in again – that a Dawnwalker sequel could strip out this mechanic and still inexorably be a Dawnwalker game – I’ve interrogated my own assumptions. I wonder if we’ve been giving anyone who’d roll back a couple of 0s on the odometer too hard a ride. Is the example of the “irresponsible modder”, someone incapable of understanding that developer intent should supersede any possible alteration, a fantasy?
points: Modders are extending The Blood of Dawnwalker's 30-day time limit to allow more time to complete every questline.
But while this goes against the developer's vision, it shouldn't be seen as vandalism.

articles.title: Lollipop Chainsaw Is Getting An Official Live-Action Movie Prequel
articles.summary: Following the announcement of a new Lollipop Chainsaw video game, Dragami Games has also confirmed that a live-action prequel movie is in the works. James Gunn, the filmmaker who worked on the original game, doesn't appear to be involved in the adaptation as he continues to work on his new…
body: Deadline revealed the existence of the Lollipop Chainsaw movie on Sept. 18, hot off the announcement of Lollipop Chainsaw 2 Back2Back at Tokyo Game Show earlier in the week. Its report describes the movie as a prequel to the first game and an "R-rated action comedy" about the series' protagonist, Juliet Starling.

It's still early days for the project, so it currently just has a creative and production team consisting of a grab bag of international filmmakers and producers. Dragami Games told Deadline that it's "pleased to be working with such an experienced and passionate international team — one that understands what makes Lollipop Chainsaw special while embracing the opportunity to create something new." No director or major Western film studio appears to be attached to the Lollipop Chainsaw movie at this time.

articles.title: As Fans Flood the World of Warcraft: Forever Beta, Dev Says It's Putting Up 'The Craziest Numbers I've Seen in 17 Years Working at Blizzard'
articles.summary: World of Warcraft: Forever looks like it could be a smash hit after the launch of the beta was overrun with eager fans, surprising even Blizzard itself. Blizzard’s ended last weekend’s BlizzCon 2026 Opening Ceremony with the announcement of World of Warcraft: Forever, a “Classic Plus” MMO developed…
body: While Forever doesn’t launch until November 4, the beta was made available this week, and it was flooded by players. Those who did manage to get in faced disconnects. And then actually playing the game was tough due to extreme lag with looting and accepting quests. Hardly ideal.
World of Warcraft Classic developer Josh Greenfield took to X / Twitter to provide some insight into the popularity of the beta.
“Man, it was hard to sleep last night, I was so excited,” Greenfield said. “Beta has been... crazy. The craziest numbers I've seen in 17 years working at Blizzard and almost eight years on classic.

That suggests significant interest in Forever, beyond even the launch of Classic itself. As a grizzled veteran of World of Warcraft’s early years, I remember well the brutal login queues most players would face when the groundbreaking MMO launched late 2004 and early 2005. Forever is rekindling those memories for me.

articles.title: Paramount's New High Fantasy Epic is Already the Streaming Sleeper Hit of 2026
articles.summary: Sega has been making video games since 1973 and owns the rights to everything from modern hit franchises like Yakuza and Persona to arcade mainstays like Crazy Taxi and Streets of Rage. The possibilities were endless. McMahan didn't hesitate. He chose Golden Axe.
body: Mike McMahan was working as a script doctor on the Sonic the Hedgehog movies when he received an incredible offer: A Sega executive approached him and asked if there were any other properties the storied game studio owned that he'd want to adapt into a series.
"I'm very old," McMahan tells Polygon by way of explaining his somewhat surprising choice. "When the NES came out, that was amazing for me, and before then, I played an insane amount of Golden Axe."

For the unfamiliar, Golden Axe is a series of beat-'em-up fantasy video games released by Sega. The first one debuted in 1989 as an arcade cabinet. Seven sequels and spinoffs followed, with the last being 1995's Golden Axe: The Duel, though a new game was announced by Sega at the 2023 Game Awards and is seemingly still in development.

In other words, Golden Axe is not exactly a hot commodity, but that didn't stop McMahan, whose memory of the game dates back to his time at a Chicago summer camp where Golden Axe and a few other arcade cabinets were rigged up so you could play them for free.
points: Sega has been making video games since 1973 and owns the rights to everything from modern hit franchises like Yakuza and Persona to arcade mainstays like Crazy Taxi and Streets of Rage.

articles.title: Marvel's Wolverine Update Tones Down Its Most Controversial Feature
articles.summary: Compared to the typical big-budget, PlayStation-exclusive video game, the reception to Marvel's Wolverine has been much more muted. One of the biggest complaints is how much Marvel's Wolverine hand-holds players when directing them where to go next.
body: Late at night on Sept. 18, Insomniac Games released hotfix v1.001.005 for Marvel's Wolverine. A support page on Insomniac's website mentions that this update not only fixes some crash-causing issues, but also "adjusts the presentation of the Scent Trails and Audio Sense indicators, including reduced opacity to make these visuals less intense."

Players didn't take long to notice the update had rolled out. A post by X user and PlayStation influencer Radec highlighted how it changed. The scent trail used to be a bold, bright blue line, really clashing with the realistic environments of the game's already linear levels. Now, it looks cloudier and like less of a defined line, while still showing players where they need to go.

articles.title: Marvel's Wolverine Developer Nerfs Scent Trails and Audio Sense Indicators After 'Fart Gas' Backlash
articles.summary: Insomniac has released an update for Marvel’s Wolverine that nerfs the “fart gas” that had become such a talking point even before the game’s release. The debate around this was rekindled following the publication of Marvel’s Wolverine reviews earlier this month, with The Washington Post journalist…
body: There was some confusion online about the ability to turn this feature off via accessibility options. Insomniac’s official list of accessibility options for Wolverine includes a “Chase Assist,” which lets you toggle reduced movement speed for targets during chase sequences, but it does not turn off the trail. Other navigation toggles do not turn off the scent trail either.

Ahead of Wolverine’s release, Insomniac’s director of community and marketing, James Stevenson, took to social media to explain that Logan's scent trail is baked into the way the mutant's powers work.

“The scent trail isn’t always on,” he clarified. “It represents Logan’s canon mutant super senses and elite tracking ability. It only is there when he’s tracking a specific scent / sound (a person, whisky, or another clue scent) - story/mission moments or when he catches whiff of a collectible.”

Referencing previous discourse about Final Fantasy’s yellow paint guides, some have said Logan's scent trails remove any potential skill required for chase sequences and any joy of discovery in exploration.

articles.title: Forget Your 100-Hour RPGs, Action Games Are Having a Moment
articles.summary: Gaming is a trend-based medium. Often, when a hit game turns into a generational success story, you can see it shape the industry in real-time as studios try to copy its notes. In recent history, we’ve seen that with an influx of two types of games: open-world games and Soulslikes.
body: While both of those are still very much in fashion, 2026 has seen an unexpected trend shift: Straightforward action games are having a moment. Some of the year’s best, or at least most high-profile, games are trading in vastness and RPG customization for something more focused. Call it a throwback to an older era of gaming, but it’s a welcome shift for anyone who has been put off by how demanding big-budget games have become over the years.

That charge is being led, in no small part, by Capcom. The publisher has had a statement year by releasing hit after hit that buck conventional wisdom. Rather than going big for Resident Evil Requiem, for instance, Capcom delivered a lean 11-hour game. Half of that is a straight-up action shooter, as Leon S. Kennedy blasts his way through a compact slice of Raccoon City. Not a second of gameplay goes wasted, nor is any single idea repeated more times than it needs to be.
points: Often, when a hit game turns into a generational success story, you can see it shape the industry in real-time as studios try to copy its notes.

articles.title: Lollipop Chainsaw Live-Action Movie Revealed by Dragami Games
articles.summary: A live-action Lollipop Chainsaw movie is officially in the works, developer Dragami Games has announced. The studio behind the series revival announced plans to bring Juliet Starling to the big screen as part of Tokyo Game Show 2026, with full details shared by Deadline.
body: The Lollipop Chainsaw movie will tell a prequel story set before the events of developer Grasshopper Manufacture's original bubblegum action game. It's also aimed to be an "R-rated action comedy" and will, once again, follow Juliet as the main character. Deadline also shared a brief story synopsis: "When a catastrophic zombie outbreak engulfs her school, Juliet must fight her way through the undead to save her friends, protect her family, and somehow keep her boyfriend Nick close – even if doing so ultimately requires some highly unconventional arrangements."

Dragami's film is said to be in development from an "international creative and production team" that includes Nada Holdings' Joe Teng, former ZDF Studios drama boss Robert Franke, Throne Inc MD Takafumi Yuki, Ambitious Entertainment's Kirk Shaw, and Non Stop TV's Patricio Rabuffetti. There is no word on whether original team members like Suda51 or now-DC Studios co-CEO James Gunn are involved, suggesting that, at least at this stage, they aren't attached in any capacity.

articles.title: It rules that a 27-year-old RPG, one of the greatest of all time, is still getting patches
articles.summary: A lamentable fact of our hobby is this: time marches on. Because our games have to be rendered in real-time by whatever tech we load them onto, they inevitably end up harder to run as the years wear on, and the gap grows between the tech we have and the tech the games were designed to run on.
body: You can't expect devs to maintain games in perpetuity. Unless, I guess, they happen to be the stewards of the Baldur's Gate and Planescape: Torment Enhanced Editions, which are still getting patches almost three decades after the original games released. Most recently (September 15), Planescape got a beta update to its, uh, beta update: a release candidate for an upcoming patch that will bring the game in line with the 2.7 patches some of Beamdog's other Enhanced Edition games already have.

As with those other games, the new Planescape beta (itself an addition to a previous beta from August) makes Steam Cloud saves work how they ought to: toggleable through the Steam client itself rather than via in-game options. GOG cloud saves now actually work, too and—this is probably the biggest thing—Planescape now has a UI scaling option in its settings. Leave it off and the game will keep its UI at god's own resolution, 1024x768, but if you flick it on it will adapt to better fit modern monitors. Like yours!

articles.title: HoYoverse's Nodusfall might look like Elden Ring, but there's a promising dark fantasy action game here that took me by surprise
articles.summary: Nodusfall, aesthetically at least, is about as far from a typical HoYoverse game as you can get. Gone are the bright colours, cute creatures, and bountiful anime women.
body: I'll admit to being a little worried at the beginning of my preview after learning it would consist of two boss battles fought in groups of four. After all, the majority of my co-op experience comes from RuneScape, a 25-year-old MMORPG primarily played with a mouse, and nobody wants to let their team down.

But first came the character selection. There were four options available in my demo: two focused around melee combat, two ranged. Both combat styles offered one character with healing-focused abilities which I immediately discounted - too much responsibility. The archer with a mechanical arm though? Inflicting heavy damage from a distance while taking care of any nasty surprises was definitely something I could do. Decision made, it was time to discover how my chosen role would actually play out in battle.

articles.title: This unofficial engine patch for Thief: The Dark Project adds a huge new feature that won't be in Nightdive's upcoming remaster
articles.summary: Thief: The Dark Project is one of my favourite games of all time, so naturally I am very excited for Nightdive Studios' upcoming remaster. But it's worth remembering that the community has done an excellent job supporting the game up until this point.
body: And if you thought an official remaster might put such efforts to an end, think again. Not to be outdone by Nightdive, NewDark's creator just released a new version of the overhaul which adds a radical new feature to Thief—dynamic shadows.

Yep, NewDark 1.29 introduces hardware transform & lighting to the Dark Engine, opening the door to GPU-driven effects in Thief's gothic steampunk world. Chief among these is shadows that are dynamically cast by moving objects—guards, doors, even master thief Garrett himself.

The update's effects were shown off in a YouTube video by Thief fan Bentraxx. What's particularly interesting about the dynamic shadows is not simply how they look, but the mechanical implications they have. For example, opening a door between a dark corridor and a well-lit room will flood the former with light, while opened doors create shadows behind them, meaning Garrett can now use doors to create hiding spaces.
points: Thief: The Dark Project is one of my favourite games of all time, so naturally I am very excited for Nightdive Studios' upcoming remaster.

articles.title: CD Projekt says abandoning its in-house engine for The Witcher 4 had nothing to do with Cyberpunk 2077's technical woes: 'The dream of the company was actually never to make technology'
articles.summary: We still don't know a huge amount about The Witcher 4. But we do know it represents two big changes for the series thus far. The first change is, of course, that Ciri will replace Geralt as the lead character. The second is that CD Projekk will replace its in-house REDengine with Unreal Engine 5.
body: There's been considerable speculation as to why CDP is abandoning tech that's delivered some of the most cutting-edge visuals of the last decade, with some fans suggesting that Cyberpunk 2077 's difficult development and compromised initial release might be a factor. But the studio's co-CEO Michał Nowakowski has formally dismissed this suggestion, stating the decision had more to do with CD Projekt's general ambitions than Cyberpunk specifically.

Speaking on the Deconstructor of Fun podcast (via GamesRadar+ ), Nowakowski addressed the claim that Cyberpunk was the straw that broke REDengine's back: "A lot of people think like this, but this is a bit of a false assumption," he explained. "Because the issue with Cyberpunk was not really REDengine itself.

articles.title: Indie Dev Says “AI” Voice In His Game Was Actually His Wife
articles.summary: Someone playing Refractive Entertainment's recently released action-RPG Luminary for less than an hour accused the team of using AI for the game's only voiced character. The player said the voice "killed it" for them. There was just one problem: It wasn't AI.
body: Refractive Entertainment launched Luminary into Steam Early Access on August 11. It's a resource-gathering action-adventure sandbox with an art style that's giving Fable meets Immortals Fenyx Rising. It's cute-looking and well-received, with a "Mostly Positive" rating out of almost 350 Steam reviews. But for an indie developer who says his game's success lives and dies by its Steam review score, one particular negative review caught the creative director's attention.

On September 10, user NyteKnyte posted a short Steam review after only 0.4 hours with the game to say that Luminary looked good but "the awful AI-generated voice killed it" for them. "Feels off, like an AI game," NyteKnyte said in their review. "Hopefully its temporary and gets better, but [the AI voice] killed it for me."
Not long after this review hit the game's Steam page, Refractive Entertainment responded, saying that the “awful AI-generated voice” that NyteKnyte decried was actually the creative director's wife.

articles.title: Dune Awakening now has a solo mode for players put off by its MMO leanings, while Funcom has adjusted progression so 'you don't have to lose things anymore'
articles.summary: Dune Awakening was lauded for its survivalist take on Frank Herbert's sci-fi epic when it was released last year, but there's one element of Funcom's sci-fi adventure that's proved consistently controversial, and that's its MMO-adjacent elements.
body: Now though, in a move that would please Harkonnens galaxy-wide, Funcom has made it so you can keep Arrakis all to yourself. Dune Awakening's long-sought after single-player mode has arrived. Update 1.5 introduces a tweaked version of Awakening suitable for solo play, while also adjusting Arrakis in a bunch of other ways to make it generally more accessible and less punishing.

Funcom has changed several core mechanics to make solo mode work, chiefly retooling multiplayer-reliant systems so they can work independently. The player-driven market known as the Exchange now functions as a sci-fi supermarket offering a wide-array of items for players to pick up as they please. Meanwhile, its Landsraad political system simulates rival guilds automatically, ensuring it "progresses even without player participation". Finally, while not player-driven, Coriolis storms have been softened so that players can maintain progress in the Deep Desert, though Function cautions that these storms remain "very dangerous."

Construct towering cityscapes, fine-tune their look and layout, and give every structure its own distinctive character.
Miniopolis will be available on PC (via Steam).
videos.author: IGN
